newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar weakens further, sterling bruised.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar weakens further, sterling bruised.

text.p: The dollar's powerful run slowed on Tuesday as traders pocketed profits, and the pound was bruised further by talk in some quarters that British interest rates were unlikely to be increased soon.
European equity markets got off to a healthy start, with some approaching record levels, but they fell back in the early afternoon, rattled by an unsettled opening on Wall Street.
The U.S. currency, which surged to a seven-and-a-half year high of 1.8490 marks at one stage on Monday, shed two pfennigs by Tuesday afternoon to 1.8285 marks.
Dealers attributed the fresh dollar weakness to end-of-the-month profit-taking and questions about whether German officials could intervene to support their ailing currency.
The U.S. currency reacted only marginally to data issued on Tuesday showing that American employment costs rose 0.8 percent in the second quarter -- exactly in line with estimates.

"It's the end of the month, we've had a huge move in the past two-and-a-half weeks and people are putting a little money in the bank," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer & Co in New York.
"But somewhere along the way people will come in and put on some fresh dollar positions," he predicted.
The profit-taking by some traders was prompted by reports suggesting Germany might be willing to intervene or switch to a variable rate repo in order to defend the mark.

In an interview with the German daily Berliner Zeitung, Rolf Peffekoven, a member of the Council of Economic Advisors, dubbed Germany's "five wise men," said Group of Seven industrialized nations could come to the aid of the mark, which sunk to its lowest level against the dollar.

The dollar, up five percent against the mark in the last three weeks, has prospered because of a growing conviction that Europe's planned single currency would be launched with a broad group of countries, making for a weak euro.
Sterling, which shed five pfennigs against the mark on Monday, fell another three pfennigs to 2.9785 by midafternoon.

Some dealers said the pound's plunge from its 25 percent increase over the last year against a trade-weighted basket of currencies looked more like a correction than the first leg of a big sell-off, analysts said.

"The moves we have seen this week are not based on anything solid. The near-term risks are still that rates are going to go up and sterling/mark will test 3.0-3.05 marks," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN AMRO.

The downturn was partly prompted by talk that the Bank of England , which has hiked interest rates three times since May, might hold off another interest rate rise at a meeting next week. Complaints from UK exporters have been getting louder about the harmful strength of sterling.

A counter-argument, that an August rate rise was likely, came in figures on Tuesday showing a record rise in personal credit, which suggested British consumers are borrowing heavily as well as spending freely.

"The big headache facing the Bank is how can it slow down the consumer without driving the pound up. We think it will raise rates by a quarter point and hint that it may then pause for a while," said James Barty, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

The falling pound, making British exports more competitive, helped the London bourse at the start. The FTSE-100 index was lifted by engineering stocks which bounced in response to the pound's fall sharp fall but most gains were eroded by the a negative opening on Wall Street.
"There's a knee-jerk reaction from the engineers in particular, which have been hit the hardest," one dealer said. "Sterling has lifted the pressure on these exporting companies."
In Frankfurt, floor trade, which ended before New York opened, finished with gains of 0.25 percent, but dealings on the after-hours computerised IBIS index down 0.7 percent, hurt by Wall Street.
"The pressure from America became too much," said one Frankfurt dealer. "They are lower, so we are lower too."
Paris stocks, which hit an intra-day high on Monday, lost earlier hefty gains, unsettled by Wall Street.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8285 marks and 117.72 yen compared to 1.8466 and 117.70 in late trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index up 0.6 points at 4,863.2.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended up 10.53 points in bourse trade at 4,381.69.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 0.13 points at 3,022.07.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $326.55, compared to $327.50 at Monday's close. Silver was down two cents at $4.37.
